text: Scusi, non ho capito.
why: Exact repeat of examples[0], so it adds no new case of non before a verb.
fix: Use a different verb with non in front, e.g. "Scusi, non ho sentito il prezzo."

text: Può dirlo in inglese?
why: dirlo has lo stuck to the verb, so it doesn't show what the notice says (can + the basic form of the verb).
fix: "Può parlare più piano, per favore?" or "Può scrivere il prezzo?"

text: To say “Sorry?” Italians say Come? or Scusi?
why: This is about asking someone to repeat, a second point; it doesn't help with asking about words.
fix: Something about learning words on the spot, e.g. "People here are usually happy to tell you a word and spell it out."

text: Non sai dire una parola in italiano. Cosa chiedi? → Come si dice “receipt” in italiano?
why: The ask never names the word, so the learner can't arrive at the expected answer.
fix: Name the word in the ask: "Vuoi la parola italiana per “receipt”. Cosa chiedi?"

text: Vuoi scrivere una parola nuova. Cosa chiedi? → Come si scrive?
why: The ask gives away the verb (scrivere), so most of the answer is already there.
fix: Ask without the verb, e.g. "Hai sentito una parola nuova e vuoi sapere le lettere. Cosa chiedi?"

text: Di dove sei? → Sono di …
why: Sono di + city is the point of a1-03-5; using it here brings that point in early.
fix: Keep the practice to sono/sei/è, e.g. "Sei americano? → Sì, sono americano." or "Sei qui per lavoro? → No, sono in pensione."

text: Piacere, Rosa.
why: This line doesn't use chiamarsi at all, so it doesn't show the point.
fix: "Piacere, mi chiamo Rosa."

text: È qui in vacanza?
why: No -are verb here, and no example shows the tu form (abiti) that the notice teaches.
fix: "E tu, dove abiti?" (neighbour, tu)

text: All three answers are Abito …
why: The point is the io, tu and Lei endings, but the learner only ever says abito.
fix: Replace one item with a tu or Lei question to produce, e.g. "Chiedi a una signora anziana dove abita." → "Dove abita?"

text: Sei americano? → Sì, sono americano.
why: The ask holds the whole answer, including the ending that's being taught.
fix: Leave the nationality out of the ask, e.g. "Sei di Boston. Di che nazionalità sei?" → "Sono americano / americana."

text: Sei inglese? / Sei italiana? → No, sono americana.
why: Nothing in the ask says the speaker is a woman, so a male learner who correctly says americano gets marked wrong.
fix: Give the speaker's gender in the ask (e.g. "Sei una donna di Boston."), or accept americano / americana.

text: In quale paese abiti? → Abito in Italia.
why: The ask hands over 'in', the very preposition being practised.
fix: Ask without the preposition, e.g. "Abiti a Firenze. E il paese?" → "Abito in Italia."

text: Ed è qui in vacanza?
why: This doesn't show da + present.
fix: "Da quanto tempo è in Italia?"

text: You'll be able to say how long you've been here and why you came.
why: Promises a second point (why you came) that this lesson doesn't teach.
fix: "You'll be able to say how long you've been here."

text: Most words take un, like un caffè. Spritz takes uno, spremuta takes una, and aranciata takes un' with an apostrophe.
why: It lists one word per form instead of saying when each form is used, so the learner can't apply it to a new noun.
fix: "Un for most masculine words (un caffè), uno before s + consonant or z (uno spritz), una for feminine words (una spremuta), un' for feminine words starting with a vowel (un'aranciata)."

text: Cosa prendi la mattina al bar? / Hai sete. Cosa chiedi al barista?
why: The ask never names the item, so the article choice can't be checked, and no item practises un'.
fix: Name the noun without its article in each ask (e.g. "Ordina: spremuta.", "Ordina: aranciata.") so the learner has to supply un/uno/una/un'.

text: Standing at the banco costs less than sitting at a table.
why: Nothing to do with plurals.
fix: Leave it empty, or tie it to ordering for two, e.g. "With a friend you often order two of the same: due caffè."

text: Per me un cappuccino e un cornetto.
why: Not vorrei: a second way to order slipped into the vorrei lesson.
fix: "Vorrei un cappuccino e un cornetto."

text: Per me plus the item is another friendly way to order.
why: Teaches a second point instead of explaining vorrei.
fix: Cut the sentence: "Vorrei plus the item is a polite way to ask for anything, and you can use it just as it is."

text: Italians have cappuccino in the morning, so it's a breakfast order.
why: Culture about cappuccino, not about asking politely with vorrei.
fix: "Vorrei works anywhere you ask for something: the bar, the market, a shop."

text: ventuno, ventotto, trentatré, duecento
why: The notice and practice[2] teach mille and duemila, but no example shows them.
fix: Replace one example with "Sono duemila euro." or "Sono mille euro."

text: Quant'è?
why: The mission practises asking the total, not saying a price in euros.
fix: Say a price back to check it, e.g. "Tre euro e venti?"

text: If you just point, say Quanto costa? with nothing before it.
why: Says 'before' where the point is that nothing comes after costa, which confuses the word-order rule just given.
fix: "If you just point, say Quanto costa? with nothing after it."

text: Examples[2–3], notice, context and practice[2] cover Ha moneta? / non ho spiccioli / Pago in contanti / Ecco a Lei
why: Half the lesson is about getting change and handing over money, not posso + infinitive.
fix: Keep only posso + infinitive: examples like "Posso pagare con il bancomat?" and "Posso pagare dopo?"; notice about posso + basic verb only; context about cards ("Shops take cards, but small stalls prefer cash for small amounts."); practice[2] → "Hai solo contanti. Cosa chiedi?" → "Posso pagare in contanti?"

text: Come chiedi se puoi pagare con la carta? → Posso pagare con la carta?
why: The ask holds the whole answer (puoi pagare con la carta), so only puoi→posso is left to do.
fix: Give the situation instead: "Hai solo la carta. Cosa chiedi alla cassa?" / "Non hai la carta, solo soldi. Cosa chiedi?"
